title: Streamline Villa
description: Semester 03 — Streamline Villa, Malé: a five-storey mixed-use building shaped by fluidity and curved balconies.
lead: Streamline Villa is a five-storey mixed-use building designed for an urban site in Malé. The project explores fluidity and movement through curved balcony forms, creating a softer architectural expression within the dense urban context.
summary: A five-storey mixed-use building exploring fluidity and movement through curved balcony forms, giving a softer architectural expression within a dense urban context.
cv_line: Malé · Five-storey mixed-use building with curved balcony façade

hero.alt: Streamline Villa facade with curved balconies

head.title: Concept
head.intro: The concept explores fluidity and movement through flowing architectural forms. Curved elements shape the façade and building form, while ocean-inspired colours create a sense of calm and flow.

blocks.label: Site
blocks.alt: Site location: Maldives, Malé and the site

blocks.label: Concept — fluidity
blocks.text: Curved lines soften the building’s edge, carrying a sense of continuous movement into the tight grid of Malé.

items.caption: Flow study — curved lines explore movement and fluidity
Façade pattern — flowing lines shape the balconies
Final application — curved balconies create visual flow

head.title: Design
head.intro: Retail and arrival on the ground floor, entertainment on the first, residences on the typical floors and a pool terrace on the roof, each level organised through the same flowing language.

blocks.label: Bubble diagrams
blocks.alt: Bubble diagrams for ground, first, typical and terrace floors

blocks.label: Form development
blocks.alt: Basic mass, curve introduced, form opened, spatial development

head.title: Floor
head.intro: Four plan types, each paired with a sectional axonometric. The curve moves in from the façade to shape lobbies, rooms and the terrace pool.

head.title: Final
head.intro: Ocean-blue balconies wrap the building in continuous, overlapping curves, giving the street a softer edge and every home an outdoor space.
